adjustment.convention: adjusted(t) = close(t) * PROD(multiplier for ex_date > t); the most recent close is unadjusted and history is scaled to meet it
adjustment.look_ahead: none in any return: the factor cancels except for actions inside the window, all of which had occurred by the end of it. Levels do carry future actions, and no frozen factor reads a level.

track_a.label: V1.0 price-observable validation
track_a.not: This is NOT full V1/V2 validation. It covers the two factors the archive can reconstruct and no others.

momentum.definition: Absolute 12-1 momentum, volatility-adjusted: return from 252 trading days before formation to 21 days before, divided by annualised daily volatility over that window, through tanh. Read from alpha_model, not restated here.

track_a.exploratory_warning: 18 exploratory comparisons were made by regime and liquidity. No correction is applied to them and none should be read as a finding; they are cut from the same 92 months as the primary tests and cannot be independent of them.

track_b.label: UNTESTABLE WITH CURRENT PIT DATA

quality.needs: Point-in-time fundamentals: return on equity, debt/equity, margins and interest cover AS REPORTED on each formation date, with the filing date attached so a figure is only visible after it was published.
quality.why_not: The archive holds prices. Today's ROE applied to a February 2025 formation scores the company on information that did not exist then, and on a balance sheet that has since been restated.

value.needs: Point-in-time earnings, book value and sales per share, with filing dates. Price is already available, so a historical P/E needs only the denominator.
value.why_not: Today's EPS against a 2025 price is not the multiple anyone traded on; it embeds two years of subsequent earnings news.

growth.needs: A history of reported revenue and earnings growth by filing date.
growth.why_not: Same reason as quality and value, and worse: growth is measured across periods, so a single restatement moves every historical observation.

sentiment.needs: An archive of news headlines with publication timestamps, scored by the same FinBERT model, so the score at a formation date reflects only articles published before it.
sentiment.why_not: News is fetched live. There is no stored history of what was published when, so a historical sentiment score cannot be reconstructed at all — not approximately, not at all.

composite_alpha_and_signals.needs: All of the above. The composite is a weighted sum, so it is reconstructible exactly when its inputs are.
composite_alpha_and_signals.why_not: Strong Buy / Buy / Neutral / Sell / Strong Sell are thresholds on the composite. With four of six inputs unavailable historically, the labels cannot be reconstructed, and a version built from the two available factors would be a different model wearing the same names.

sector_attribution.needs: A point-in-time sector classification covering delisted companies — an industry mapping as it stood on each date.
sector_attribution.why_not: The platform's sector map is today's and covers only currently-listed names, so using it would import both look-ahead and survivorship into every sector bucket.

market_cap_strata.needs: Historical shares outstanding, to turn a close into a market capitalisation.
market_cap_strata.why_not: The bhavcopy files carry price and volume but not shares outstanding. Traded value is reported instead and called liquidity, because a Large/Mid/Small label derived from turnover would be a guess with a precise-sounding name.

track_b.rule_applied: No historical value was substituted for a missing one. Today's fundamentals, today's news, today's sector map and today's market caps were all available and all refused, because using any of them would score a past date on information from after it.

multiple_testing.note: Two factors by four horizons were declared before the results were read. Horizons without enough non-overlapping windows are excluded from the correction rather than counted as passes or failures.

method.identity: Securities are resolved identities, chained across renames and ISIN changes, the same keying the corrected backtest uses.
method.excess: Excess is against the equal-weighted return of the eligible universe that month, not an index. It removes the market move without introducing an external series the archive cannot verify.
method.delistings: A security with no price at the horizon is marked -100%, matching the frozen backtest.
method.buckets: Quintiles are formed within each month, so a bucket is a cross-sectional rank and never a comparison across time.
method.clustering: Every interval and p-value is computed on the effective sample size — observations divided by a design effect estimated by ANOVA across formation months. Stocks picked in the same month share that month's market and are not independent.
method.regimes: Trend is the trailing 3-month equal-weight market return, above +5.0% Bull, below -5.0% Bear, otherwise Sideways. Volatility is the annualised trailing 3-month figure against 20%. Both use only months before the formation date. These thresholds are conventions fixed in advance, not fitted.

limits: 92 formation months over a single market period. Closes are corrected for splits, bonuses and dividends (19047 corporate actions applied, 1233 could not be; see 'adjustment'), and traded value is left as printed. Nothing here establishes a durable edge, and a result that survives correction over 92 months would still need out-of-sample confirmation.
